passages.original: 523 : Interlocutio hoc ipsum significans ex rescripto Principia superius recitato. Rescriptum istud ad Eumalium vicarium Africae, laudat Augustinus in Breviculo Collat. 5, n. 57 : et lib. post Collationem, n. 56, ubi datum dicit Sabino et Rufino consulibus, quarto idus novembres (a). Ipsam quoque Constantini sententiam secundum Cæcilianum dictam ex eodem rescripto affert in lib. 3 contra Crescon., n. 82 : Insero adhuc, ait, et verba Constantini ex litteris ejus ad Eumalium vicarium, ubi se inter partes cognovisse, et innocentem Cæcilianum comperisse testatur.
passages.english: 523: An interlocutory statement signifying this very thing, from the rescript of the Emperor recited above. This rescript, addressed to Eumalius, vicar of Africa, Augustine cites in the Summary of the Conference 5, n. 57, and in the book after the Conference, n. 56, where he says it was issued in the consulship of Sabinus and Rufinus, on the fourth day before the Ides of November (a). He also adduces Constantine's actual sentence, pronounced in favour of Caecilian, from the same rescript in book 3 against Cresconius, n. 82: "I insert further," he says, "the words of Constantine too, from his letter to Eumalius the vicar, where he testifies that he heard the case between the parties and found Caecilian innocent."
passages.notes: "Principia" is evidently a scanning error for "Principis" (the Emperor); translated accordingly. "(a)" is the edition's footnote mark. "Breviculo Collat." = Augustine's Breviculus Collationis cum Donatistis; "lib. post Collationem" = Ad Donatistas post Collationem; "contra Crescon." = Contra Cresconium. The date given corresponds to 10 November 316.
